chunks: O Allah, and this is the station of one who has singled You out with the Oneness that is due to You,
and has not regarded anyone else as deserving of these praises and eulogies except You,
and I have a need for You which nothing can mend its destitution except Your generosity,
nor revive it from its deficiency except Your bounty and munificence,
so grant us in this station Your pleasure,
and make us free from stretching hands to anyone other than You,
"Certainly, You are powerful over every thing."
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication of Imam Ali regarding divine unity and human need?
ai.summary: Found within the 'Al-Ashbaah' chapter of Nahj al-Balagha, this supplication highlights Imam Ali’s profound theological insight by linking the cosmic order to the spiritual station of Tawhid, where God is recognized as the sole object of worship and praise. It underscores the Shia concept of human existential poverty (al-faqar al-ilahi), asserting that only divine grace can rectify human insufficiency, thereby fostering total reliance (Tawakkul) on Allah alone. This reflection serves as a practical guide for believers to cultivate inner richness by detaching from worldly dependencies and seeking only divine pleasure.

en.sayed-ali-raza: O my Allāh! here stands one who has singled Thee with Oneness that is Thy due
and has not regarded any one deserving of these praises and eulogies except Thee.
My want towards Thee is such that nothing except Thy generosity can cure its destitution,
nor provide for its need except Thy obligation and Thy generosity.
So do grant us in this place Thy will
and make us free from stretching hands to anyone other than Thee.
“Certainly, Thou art powerful over every thing.” (Qur’ān, 66:8)
